`drivers/usb/typec/class.c:904-912`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner, struct device *dev)
{
	sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));  // removes reverse link
	sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");                // class.c:909  <-- 'typec' link
	...
}
```

The symlink literally named `"typec"` is created in the **USB device directory** at `class.c:892` (`sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec")`). So when removing it at `class.c:909`, `dev` is the **USB child device (`usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev`)**, and `dev->kobj.sd` is the directory the link lives in. That is the parent passed to `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns`. It being NULL means **the USB child device's sysfs/kernfs node was already torn down** while it was still referenced from the port.

## 4. Where `dev->kobj.sd` becomes NULL

`fs/sysfs/dir.c:79-96` (`sysfs_remove_dir`) nulls `kobj->sd` as part of node teardown:

```c
	spin_lock(&sysfs_symlink_target_lock);
	kobj->sd = NULL;    // dir.c:96
	spin_unlock(...);
```

That runs in the device-teardown path `device_del()` (`drivers/base/core.c:3893` `kobject_del(&dev->kobj)` → `sysfs_remove_dir`). So once a USB child device is deleted, its `kobj.sd` is NULL.

## 6. Why does `port->usb*_dev` point at an already-removed node?

`port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` are set by `typec_partner_attach` (`class.c:2144-2162`, called from `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2722`) and cleared by `typec_partner_deattach` (`class.c:2169-2185`, called from `drivers/usb/core/hub.c:2363`) and by `typec_unregister_partner` (`class.c:1186,1190`).

The USB child device's *actual* teardown is `device_del()` in the hub removal path — which runs after `typec_deattach` but is **not** serialized with the typec `partner_link_lock`. That lock protects only the *pointer field*, not the lifetime of the pointed-to device/kernfs node. Concretely, on this Dell the connector cycles at boot: the UCSI disconnect event is merely queued on the workqueue; in the interim the USB subsystem has already deleted the USB child device and its sysfs directory (`sd = NULL`), yet `port->usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` still holds the stale reference. `typec_unregister_partner` then blindly unlinks a "typec" symlink from a `kobj` whose `sd` is gone → parent NULL → `-ENOENT` → warning.

(The same failure also exists even in the clean teardown ordering at `ucsi.c:2147`, where `ucsi_unregister_partner` runs before `typec_unregister_port`.)
